# Summary of the Green Party Manifesto 2005

The 2005 Green Party Manifesto presents a comprehensive vision for transforming Britain into a sustainable society built on principles of social, economic, and environmental justice.

## Economic Policy

The manifesto proposes significant wealth redistribution through progressive taxation, including a 50% rate on earnings over £50,000 and 60% on earnings over £100,000. VAT would be replaced with eco-taxes linked to environmental impact. The party advocates economic localisation to counter globalisation, opposing UK entry to the euro and supporting community banks, credit unions, and local currencies. A Land Value Tax would replace Council Tax to address land ownership inequality.

## Climate and Energy

Adopting the "Contraction and Convergence" framework, the Greens target a 20% carbon dioxide emissions reduction by 2010, with 85% by 2030. They propose a carbon tax, increasing renewable energy to 40% by 2020, and closing nuclear power stations. Investment would shift from nuclear to renewable sources including solar, wind, and wave power.

## Welfare Reform

Central to the manifesto is the Citizen's Income—an unconditional, universal payment covering basic needs without means-testing. A Citizen's Pension would provide guaranteed retirement income linked to average earnings. The party supports reducing working hours, improving childcare, and increasing affordable housing through various measures including Land Value Tax reform.

## Health and Education

The NHS would return to founding principles of universal care, rejecting privatisation and Public-Private Partnerships. Prescription charges, eye tests, and dental treatment would become free. Education funding would increase, tuition fees would be abolished, maintenance grants restored, and SATs scrapped in favour of individualised learning plans.

## Transport

The manifesto prioritises sustainable transport, targeting a 10% reduction in road traffic by 2010. £30 billion would be diverted from road building to public transport. Rail and tube networks would return to public ownership. Aviation fuel tax would be introduced, and airport expansion resisted.

## Environment

A Zero Waste Strategy would target 60% domestic waste recycling by 2010. The party would establish an Environmental Protection Commission, strengthen pollution controls, and apply the precautionary principle to technologies like genetic modification. Animal rights would be protected, including banning blood sports and ending live animal exports.

## Food and Agriculture

An Organics Target Bill would aim for 30% organic production by 2012. The Common Agricultural Policy would be replaced with support for local food markets and sustainable farming. Genetically modified food would be banned, and supermarket anti-competitive behaviour tackled.

## Crime and Justice

The approach emphasises prevention through stronger communities, improved urban design, and increased youth facilities. Community policing would expand, restorative justice programmes would be introduced, and strict gun control legislation implemented. National ID cards are opposed.

## Democracy

Constitutional reforms include proportional representation for Westminster and local elections, an elected House of Lords, devolved regional government, and a written constitution. Local government powers would be enhanced.

## International Policy

The manifesto advocates withdrawal from Iraq, nuclear disarmament, and reducing military spending to EU averages. Overseas aid would increase to 1% of GNI, and debt cancellation would be pursued for the 52 poorest countries. The WTO would be reformed through a General Agreement on Sustainable Trade favouring local economies. The party opposes the proposed EU constitution while supporting continued EU membership with reforms.
